title: Render svg preview images in File Explorer is too slow
author: sebasav182

status.label: Performance design investigation queued
status.detail: The report has a clear 50+ SVG workload and screenshot, but no maintainer action is defensible until profiling separates process startup, rendering, and Explorer scheduling costs.

next_action.label: Continue SVG thumbnail performance design
next_action.reason: Develop profiled design evidence before exposing an approve_design action.

judgment.rationale: The workload and latency are clear enough for design work, and source inspection identifies the synchronous per-thumbnail external-renderer path as the first area to profile.
evidence: The reporter says the first visit to a directory with at least 50 SVG files renders thumbnails one by one at about 4-5 seconds each.
The issue has no comments, assignees, or linked fix as of the forced rerun.
SvgThumbnailProvider::GetThumbnail writes each stream to a temporary SVG, launches PowerToys.SvgThumbnailProvider.exe, waits with WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE), then loads a temporary BMP.
judgment.recommended_action: Continue a profiled implementation-grade design covering process reuse or in-process rendering, timeout/cancellation, Explorer concurrency, cache behavior, and representative SVG throughput tests.

issue_context.summary: SVG thumbnail generation is extremely slow for a folder of many files, and the provider pays a synchronous external-process and temporary-file handoff for each thumbnail.
known_information: The author supplied version 0.100.2, Windows 11 25H2, workload size, observed latency, and a screenshot.
The delay occurs on the first directory visit while thumbnails are generated.
The native shell thumbnail provider synchronously waits for a managed renderer process for each request.
No comments, assignees, cross-references, or closing PRs are attached to the issue.
inferences: Per-request process startup and temporary-file handoff may be a major cost, but profiling is needed before calling that the root cause.
Explorer scheduling and cache behavior may also contribute, so unbounded parallel rendering would be risky without design validation.
issue_context.analysis: This is actionable for design investigation, not for an immediate maintainer action. The artifact should not expose an approve_design action until there is measured evidence and a concrete implementation plan.
initial_investigation: Forced 2026-09-02 pass read the complete issue body, current labels, empty assignee list, and timeline links; there are no issue comments or linked work.

Read src/modules/previewpane/SvgThumbnailProviderCpp/SvgThumbnailProvider.cpp: GetThumbnail creates a temporary SVG, ShellExecuteEx launches PowerToys.SvgThumbnailProvider.exe, waits indefinitely, and reads the generated BMP.
Confirmed this pass found a plausible cost center but no profiler data, duplicate, assignee, or existing fix PR.

Forced second pass on 2026-09-02 re-read the full report, labels, empty assignee list, and timeline and checked provider-file history; no newer performance fix or duplicate changes the need for measured investigation.

information_gaps.why_needed: The design must target the dominant cost and avoid unsafe speculative parallelism in a shell extension.
information_gaps.information: A representative profile on current stable/main separating process startup, rendering, disk handoff, cache hit/miss, and Explorer request scheduling time.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Use provider logging/profiling with a representative 50-file SVG directory during full design investigation.
